rules.message: Wolverine 6 forbids service location. A plain AddDbContext makes the first message that injects the context throw InvalidServiceLocationException.
rules.fix: Use opts.Services.AddDbContextWithWolverineIntegration<T>(...) inside UseWolverine, or AddDbContext<T>(..., optionsLifetime: ServiceLifetime.Singleton). Suppress the rule in a project without Wolverine handlers.

rules.message: Dynamic code generation compiles each handler with Roslyn at run time: a slow start, more memory, and errors only at the first message (decision MSG-13).
rules.fix: Set x.Production.GeneratedCodeMode = TypeLoadMode.Static in CritterStackDefaults, run 'dotnet run -- codegen write' in CI, and commit Internal/Generated/.

rules.message: MassTransit, NServiceBus, and MediatR interfaces do not work in Wolverine. Wolverine finds handlers by convention.
rules.fix: Write a public static class whose name ends in Handler, with a static Handle method that takes the message and returns the cascading messages.
match: public sealed class Handler : IRequestHandler<GetOrder, OrderDto>
nomatch: public static OrderShipped Handle(ShipOrder command, OrdersDbContext db)

rules.message: RestoreV5Defaults turns the Wolverine 5 defaults back on, also service location. It hides registrations that the code generator cannot see through.
rules.fix: Fix the registrations: AddDbContextWithWolverineIntegration, AddScoped<IFoo, Foo>(). For one opaque type, use opts.CodeGeneration.AlwaysUseServiceLocationFor<T>() with a reason.

rules.message: A fixed wait for a handler is slow when it is long and flaky when it is short.
rules.fix: Use a tracked session: await host.TrackActivity().Timeout(30.Seconds()).InvokeMessageAndWaitAsync(message), or ExecuteAndWaitAsync for an HTTP call.
nomatch: await Task.Delay(500, ct); // poll interval inside a wait loop with a deadline

rules.message: Wolverine uses System.Text.Json by default. Newtonsoft.Json in new code adds a second serializer and its own rules (decision MSG-11).
rules.fix: Keep System.Text.Json. Use Newtonsoft only for interop with an existing publisher that needs it, with a reason.
